title: SpaceX calls for better coordination in orbit after near-misses with Starlink
gist: SpaceX's Michael Nicolls used the IAC to call for universal ephemeris sharing after Starlink near-misses of tens to hundreds of meters, mainly with non-sharing (largely Chinese and Russian) satellites. Starlink (11,000+ sats) does ~1,000 avoidance maneuvers/day; Amazon Leo says data sharing is a non-issue.

insights.claim: Starlink has more than 11,000 satellites, about two-thirds of all active spacecraft in low-Earth orbit.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: SpaceX's dominance gives it outsized influence on LEO norms.

insights.claim: SpaceX has revealed plans for up to a million satellites in a Starmind constellation to deploy AI computing capacity in low-Earth orbit.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Orbital AI compute is an emerging capex theme with congestion implications.

insights.claim: Starlink satellites perform about 1,000 collision avoidance maneuvers per day.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Collision avoidance is an ongoing operational cost of megaconstellations.

insights.claim: Nicolls argues that even though daily collision risk is tiny, the law of large numbers means a collision will eventually happen.
insights.speaker: Michael Nicolls
insights.so_what: Tail risk of a debris cascade threatens all LEO business models.

insights.claim: Uncoordinated maneuvers by other operators have produced conjunctions with Starlink of tens to hundreds of meters.
insights.speaker: Michael Nicolls
insights.so_what: Real near-miss frequency underscores need for space traffic management.
insights.quote: these led to conjunctions of tens of meters to hundreds of meters

insights.claim: Starlink dodged about 650 active satellites from other operators in recent months, and only half come from operators sharing ephemeris with SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Half of active-satellite threats are opaque, limiting avoidance precision.

insights.claim: A SpaceX chart suggested the non-sharing problem lies largely with Chinese and Russian satellites, though some US, European and Japanese operators also decline.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Geopolitical fragmentation complicates space safety coordination.

insights.claim: No global treaties or regulations require satellites to broadcast positions or coordinate maneuvers, leaving norms to governments and companies.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Regulatory vacuum is a potential future rulemaking catalyst.
insights.locator: There’s still a long way to go

insights.claim: SpaceX's Stargaze onboard camera system now tracks about 90 percent of maneuvering satellites crossing Starlink orbits.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Proprietary space situational awareness capability is a competitive moat.

insights.claim: SpaceX lowered the entire active Starlink constellation below 500 km, and Starlink V3 satellites launched on Starship will fly at about 350 km.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Lower orbits reduce debris persistence and improve latency/service.

insights.claim: Amazon Leo head Rajeev Badyal says sharing ephemeris is a non-issue and Amazon coordinates every launch with SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Badyal
insights.so_what: Western megaconstellation operators are aligning on coordination norms.
insights.quote: So, for us, sharing ephemeris or sharing the information necessary for space safety is a non-issue

insights.claim: Amazon has 396 satellites in orbit, a 3,232-satellite first generation, FCC approval for a 4,504-satellite second generation, and a pending filing for 5,105 direct-to-device satellites.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Amazon Leo remains far behind Starlink in scale.

insights.claim: Badyal warns that coordination with China and adversaries will eventually be necessary, or it will harm everyone, especially as they reach scale.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Badyal
insights.so_what: Chinese megaconstellation scale-up raises collision and policy risk.
